chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A person who drinks wine will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, like an idol-worshipper. And whoever drinks from it once, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will not accept his prayer for forty days.

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ الْخَمْرِ: A person who drinks wine habitually
key_terms.یَلْقَی اللَّهَ: To meet Allah (on the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for drinking wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the profound spiritual degradation of wine consumption by equating the habitual drinker with an idol-worshipper, reflecting the Shia emphasis on internalizing the status of polytheism (shirk) in major sins. The specific ruling that a single sip invalidates prayers for forty days underscores the immediate ritual impurity (najāsah) and spiritual barrier created by khamr, a concept deeply rooted in both Quranic revelation and Imami jurisprudence.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Abdillah b. Ja’far from Ya’qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Abi ’Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from Sulayman b. Khalid from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
A person who drinks wine will meet Allah along with an idol-worshipper. Allah will not accept the Salaat for forty days of a person who drinks wine once.”
